title: Alivenci (Moldavian baked cornmeal and cheese custard)

ingredients.name: urdă, ricotta or fresh cottage cheese

steps: Heat the oven to 180 C and butter a baking dish about 22 cm wide.
Bring the milk to a gentle simmer and whisk in the cornmeal, then cook for about 5 minutes, stirring, until it is thick like porridge. Let it cool a little.
Beat the cheese with the sour cream, egg yolks, sugar, vanilla, lemon zest, salt and raisins until smooth, then stir in the cornmeal mixture.
Whisk the egg whites to soft peaks and fold them in gently.
Pour into the dish and bake for 35 to 40 minutes until set and golden on top.
Serve warm or cold with a spoonful of sour cream.

title: Bulz (Romanian baked cornmeal balls stuffed with cheese)

ingredients.name: salty cheese such as feta or telemea, crumbled
soft cheese or sour cream, for the filling
smoked bacon, diced and fried, to serve (optional)

steps: Cook the cornmeal in the salted boiling water for about 25 minutes, stirring often, until it makes a very thick mămăligă.
Mix the crumbled cheese with the soft cheese or a little sour cream for the filling.
Wet your hands and divide the hot mămăligă into 4 portions. Press each into a cup shape in your palm, put a quarter of the filling inside and close the cornmeal over it into a ball.
Set the balls on a baking tray lined with oiled paper and bake at 220 C for about 12 to 15 minutes until the outside forms a light crust and the cheese melts.
Serve hot with sour cream and, if you like, fried bacon.

title: Cașcaval pane (Romanian breaded fried cheese)

ingredients.name: semi-hard cheese such as cașcaval, Edam or Gouda, cut into 8 slices about 1 cm thick
cranberry, sour cherry or lingonberry sauce, to serve

steps: Chill the cheese slices so they hold their shape while frying.
Dip each slice in flour, then in the beaten egg and then press into the breadcrumbs.
Repeat the egg and breadcrumb coating once more and chill the slices for 10 minutes to set the crust.
Heat about 1.5 cm of oil in a pan to roughly 170 C.
Fry the slices for about 1 to 2 minutes per side until deep golden, without leaving them long enough for the cheese to leak.
Drain on paper towels and serve immediately with a spoonful of fruit sauce and bread or boiled potatoes.

title: Ciorbă de perișoare (Romanian sour vegetable soup with meatballs)

ingredients.name: minced pork or mixed pork and beef
onions, finely chopped (one for the meatballs, one for the soup)
sour liquid such as borș, sauerkraut brine or lemon juice with a little water, to taste
sour cream and chopped hot pepper, to serve

steps: Mix the minced meat with the rice, egg, half the parsley, one chopped onion, salt and pepper, and shape into walnut-sized balls with wet hands.
Bring the water to a boil in a large pot and add the second onion, the carrots, the parsnip and the red pepper. Simmer for 10 minutes.
Stir in the tomato paste and potatoes, then drop in the meatballs one by one, and simmer for about 20 minutes until the meatballs are cooked and the rice inside is tender.
Add the sour liquid a little at a time, tasting after each addition, until the soup is pleasantly tart, then simmer for 5 minutes more.
Season with salt and pepper and stir in the lovage or celery leaves and the remaining parsley.
Serve hot with a spoonful of sour cream and chopped hot pepper on the side.

title: Ciulama de pui (Romanian chicken in white sauce)
steps: Put the chicken in a pot with the onion, bay leaf, peppercorns and salt, cover with water and simmer gently for 35 to 40 minutes until cooked through.
Lift out the chicken, strain the stock and keep about 300 ml. Take the meat off the bones in large pieces if you prefer.
Melt the butter in a saucepan, stir in the flour and cook for 2 minutes without browning.
Whisk in the milk and 200 ml of the warm stock gradually and simmer, stirring, for 5 to 8 minutes until the sauce is smooth and creamy.
Stir in the sour cream, season with salt and pepper and add the chicken to warm through.
Sprinkle with dill and serve with mămăligă.

title: Cornulețe (Romanian crescent biscuits filled with walnuts and jam)

ingredients.name: thick jam or Turkish delight cubes, for filling

steps: Rub the butter into the flour, sugar and salt until crumbly, then mix in the sour cream and yolk and knead briefly into a soft dough. Chill, wrapped, for 1 hour.
Mix the walnuts, filling sugar and milk into a thick paste for the filling.
Roll the dough out to 3 mm thick and cut it into squares or triangles about 8 cm wide.
Place a little walnut paste and a small spoonful of jam, or a piece of Turkish delight, on the wide end of each piece, then roll up toward the tip and bend into a crescent.
Place on a lined tray and bake at 180 C for 18 to 22 minutes until pale golden.
Cool completely and dust generously with vanilla icing sugar.

title: Covrigi (Romanian pretzel-style bread rings with salt and seeds)

ingredients.name: egg yolk, beaten with 1 tbsp water, for brushing

steps: Stir the yeast and sugar into the warm water and leave it to foam for 10 minutes.
Add the flour, salt and oil and knead for 8 to 10 minutes into a smooth, elastic dough. Cover and rise for 1 hour.
Divide the dough into 10 pieces and roll each into a rope about 40 cm long, then join the ends to form a ring or twist into a loop.
Place the rings on a lined tray and let them rise for 20 minutes.
Brush with the egg wash and sprinkle with the coarse salt and seeds.
Bake at 220 C for 15 to 20 minutes until deep golden brown. Cool slightly and eat the same day.

title: Cozonac (Romanian sweet braided bread with walnuts and cocoa)
steps: Dissolve the yeast with a spoon of sugar in the warm milk and let it foam for 10 minutes.
Mix in the flour, remaining sugar, yolks, whole egg, butter, zest, vanilla and salt, and knead for 10 to 12 minutes into a soft, elastic dough. Cover and rise for 1.5 hours until doubled.
For the filling, stir the walnuts, filling sugar and cocoa into the hot milk to make a thick paste and cool it.
Divide the dough in two, roll each piece into a rectangle about 30 by 40 cm and spread with the filling, leaving a small border. Roll up each into a tight log.
Twist or braid the logs together and lay them in a lined 25 cm loaf tin or fit each log into its own tin. Let rise for another 45 minutes.
Brush with the beaten egg and bake at 180 C for about 45 to 50 minutes, covering with foil if it browns too quickly. Cool before slicing.

title: Gogoși (Romanian filled yeast doughnuts)

ingredients.name: thick jam, or sweetened cream cheese, for filling

steps: Stir the yeast and a pinch of sugar into the warm milk and let it foam for 10 minutes.
Combine with the flour, remaining sugar, eggs, butter, lemon zest, rum and salt and knead for about 10 minutes into a soft, smooth dough.
Cover and leave to rise for 1 hour until doubled, then roll to about 1.5 cm thick.
Cut out rounds about 7 cm wide, place them on a floured cloth, cover and let them rise for 20 minutes.
Fry in oil heated to about 170 C for 2 to 3 minutes per side until deep golden brown, then drain on paper towels.
Fill each doughnut with jam or sweetened cream cheese using a piping bag with a narrow nozzle, then dust generously with icing sugar.

title: Joffre cake (Romanian chocolate layer cake with ganache and buttercream)
steps: Beat the egg yolks with half the sugar until pale and thick, and in another bowl whisk the whites with the rest of the sugar to stiff peaks.
Fold the whites into the yolks, then sift over the flour and cocoa and fold gently. Bake in a lined 22 cm tin at 180 C for 25 to 30 minutes. Cool and slice into 3 layers.
For the ganache, heat the cream until just steaming, pour it over the chopped chocolate and stir until smooth. Let it cool and thicken.
Beat the butter with the icing sugar, vanilla and rum until pale and fluffy to make the buttercream.
Sandwich the sponge layers with the ganache and chill the cake for 30 minutes.
Cover the top and sides with the buttercream, smooth it and decorate with shavings of chocolate if you like. Chill for a few hours before slicing.

title: Mămăligă (Romanian cornmeal porridge with cheese and sour cream)

ingredients.name: salty crumbly cheese such as feta, to serve

steps: Bring the water and salt to a boil in a heavy pot.
Pour in the cornmeal in a slow steady stream, whisking constantly so no lumps form.
Reduce the heat to low and cook for 25 to 30 minutes, stirring with a wooden spoon every few minutes, until the mixture is very thick and pulls away from the sides of the pot.
Stir in the butter if using.
Turn the mămăligă out onto a wooden board and let it set for a couple of minutes, then slice it with a piece of thread or a wet knife.
Serve warm with crumbled cheese and sour cream, or alongside stews such as tocană.

title: Mucenici (Romanian 9 March sweet dough knots in spiced walnut syrup)
steps: Knead the flour, warm water, oil and salt into a firm smooth dough and rest it, covered, for 20 minutes.
Roll small pieces into thin ropes about 10 cm long and curl each one into a small figure of eight, or shape them into little knots.
Bring the 1.2 litres of water to a boil with the sugar, cinnamon stick and orange zest.
Drop in the dough knots and simmer for about 15 minutes until they rise to the surface and are cooked through.
Stir in the vanilla and half the walnuts and let the mixture stand and cool a little. The liquid should have thickened slightly.
Serve warm or cold in bowls, sprinkled with the remaining walnuts and a little ground cinnamon.

title: Mujdei (Romanian garlic sauce)

ingredients.name: water or a splash of vinegar
fried fish, grilled chicken or boiled potatoes, to serve

steps: Peel the garlic and pound it with the salt in a mortar until it becomes a smooth paste.
Add the oil a few drops at a time, stirring constantly in one direction, as if making mayonnaise.
Add the water or vinegar gradually, so the sauce loosens but stays thick and creamy.
Taste and add a pinch more salt if needed.
Serve at once with fried fish, grilled chicken, pork or boiled potatoes.

title: Ostropel (Romanian chicken stewed in tomato and garlic sauce)
steps: Season the chicken with salt and pepper and brown it in the oil on both sides, then remove it from the pot.
Cook the onions in the same pot over medium heat for 6 to 8 minutes until soft and golden.
Add the tomato paste and paprika and cook for a minute, then pour in the water, add the bay leaves, thyme and chilli and stir.
Put the chicken back, cover and simmer for 35 to 40 minutes, turning once, until the chicken is tender and the sauce is thick.
Stir in the garlic for the last 5 minutes and taste for seasoning.
Serve hot with mămăligă.

title: Papanași (Romanian cheese doughnuts with sour cream and cherry preserve)

ingredients.name: fresh cottage cheese or farmer's cheese, well drained
sour cherry or blueberry preserve, to serve

steps: Press the cheese through a sieve so it is smooth, then mix it with the eggs, sugar, vanilla, lemon zest and salt.
Add the semolina, flour and baking powder to form a soft dough that is not sticky, adding a little more flour if needed. Rest it for 15 minutes.
Shape the dough into rings about 8 cm across, or into balls with a smaller ball for the cap, using floured hands.
Heat the oil to about 160 C and fry the doughnuts in batches for 3 to 4 minutes per side until deep golden and cooked through.
Drain on paper towels and serve warm, topped with a generous spoonful of sour cream and the fruit preserve.

title: Pârjoale (Romanian fried meat patties with herbs)

ingredients.name: minced pork, or half pork and half beef
stale bread, soaked in milk and squeezed

steps: Mix the mince with the squeezed bread, onion, egg, mashed potato, garlic, herbs, salt and pepper and knead for a couple of minutes until the mixture holds together.
Wet your hands and shape the mixture into flattened oval patties about 1.5 cm thick.
Coat each patty lightly in flour or breadcrumbs.
Heat about 1 cm of oil in a frying pan over medium heat.
Fry the patties for 5 to 6 minutes per side until deep golden and cooked through.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot with mashed potatoes, pickles or a tomato salad.

title: Plăcinte cu brânză (Romanian cheese-filled pies)

ingredients.name: salty cheese such as feta or telemea, crumbled

steps: Knead the flour, water, egg, oil, vinegar and salt into a soft elastic dough, then wrap and rest it for 30 minutes.
Mix the feta, cottage cheese, filling eggs and dill into a thick filling. Salt only lightly, as the feta is already salty.
Divide the dough into 8 balls and roll each out very thin into a circle about 20 cm wide.
Place a generous spoonful of filling on one half of each circle, fold the other half over and press the edges firmly closed with a fork.
Set the pies on a lined tray, brush with beaten egg yolk and bake at 200 C for about 20 to 25 minutes until golden.
Serve warm, or pan-fry them in a little oil instead for a crisper crust.

title: Tocană (Romanian tomato and paprika beef stew)

ingredients.name: beef chuck, cut into 3 cm cubes

steps: Heat the oil in a heavy pot and brown the beef in batches, then set it aside.
In the same pot, cook the onions for about 8 minutes until golden, then stir in the tomato paste and paprika for 1 minute.
Return the beef, then add the garlic, bay leaf and wine and scrape up the browned bits from the base of the pot.
Pour in the hot water, add the carrot and season with salt and pepper.
Cover and simmer very gently for about 1.5 to 2 hours until the meat is tender and the sauce has thickened.
Serve hot with mămăligă.

title: Tochitură (Romanian pork cooked in its own fat, served with polenta and egg)

ingredients.name: pork shoulder or loin with some fat, cut into 2 cm cubes
crumbled salty cheese and some sour cream, to serve

steps: Season the pork with salt and pepper and put it in a wide heavy pan with a spoonful of water. Cook over medium-low heat, stirring, until the fat has rendered out of the meat.
Continue cooking until the cubes are browned all over and cooked through in their own fat, about 20 to 25 minutes.
Add the onion, bay leaf and sausage and cook for 8 minutes until the onion is soft.
Stir in the garlic and paprika, then pour in the wine and simmer for 10 minutes until the liquid has reduced to a glossy sauce.
Fry the eggs in a separate pan.
Serve the pork over wedges of mămăligă topped with a fried egg, with crumbled cheese and sour cream.
